paper_metadata.title: Constrained Optimization via Quantum Zeno Dynamics

summary: The paper proposes quantum Zeno dynamics to enforce constraints in QAOA and L-VQE, showing improved in-constraint probability and approximation ratio on 14 portfolio-optimization instances with 4-10 assets. On hardware, it demonstrates QAOA with Zeno dynamics on a Quantinuum H1-2 trapped-ion processor for two 4-asset problems, using 2000 shots and observing gains up to about 148 two-qubit gate depth in the equality-constraint case.

experiments.description: Numerical portfolio-optimization experiments comparing QAOA with Zeno dynamics against penalty-based QAOA on 14 discrete mean-variance instances (single and multiple constraints), using two mixers and varying QAOA depth.

hyperparameters.eta: depth-control hyperparameter in N_j = ceil(beta_j^2 / eta)
hyperparameters.delta: minimum in-constraint probability target parameter (used in theory and plots)
hyperparameters.p: QAOA depth varied from 1 to 5 in figures

algorithm.parameter_initialization: optimized from large number of random initial points

problem_formulation.encoding_details: one qubit per binary decision variable x_j for portfolio inclusion; constraints enforced by Zeno measurements rather than penalty-only relaxation
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x in F q x^T Sigma x - mu^T x
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Zeno projective measurements after mixer layers; penalty-term QAOA used as baseline

problem_instance.description: Discrete mean-variance Markowitz portfolio optimization with either one constraint (budget/portfolio size) or two constraints (budget plus minimum expected return) across 14 instances.

dataset_specification.description: Seven instances each for single-constraint and multiple-constraint cases; assets count ranges from 4 to 10

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical optimization over problem instances; approximation ratio and in-constraint probability reported for each QAOA depth and mixer

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Approximation ratio and in-constraint probability computed from optimized circuit outputs

speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports improved approximation ratio and feasibility versus penalty-based QAOA, but no proven asymptotic speedup over classical optimization.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Measurement count scales at most quadratically with circuit width/depth for common mixers; more generally O(polylog(dim H)) overhead for maintaining constant in-constraint probability

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No demonstrated classical-vs-quantum runtime advantage; only numerical comparisons against penalty-based QAOA on 14 portfolio instances
limiting_factors: No classical benchmark beyond penalty-based QAOA is reported
Measurement overhead and constraint-oracle cost are discussed as practical limits
Results are on small portfolio instances (4-10 assets)
